title: Reactor metrics are derived from six event-bus events, so every counter and histogram is traceable to the event that produced it
content:
Every metric uses the meter name `@powerhousedao/reactor`, and units follow OpenTelemetry semantic conventions in UCUM — curly-brace annotations like `{job}`, `{operation}`, `{event}` and `{remote}` are dimensionless counts, `ms` is a duration.

The families:

- **Queue** — `reactor.queue.jobs.enqueued` / `.dequeued` / `.completed` (READ_READY) / `.failed` (permanently) as counters, plus observable gauges `reactor.queue.depth` (pending jobs across all queues) and `reactor.queue.executing`.
- **Executor** — `reactor.executor.job.duration` (histogram, ms, RUNNING → WRITE_READY, attribute `job.success`), `reactor.executor.active_jobs`, `reactor.executor.total_processed` (attribute `job.success`), `reactor.executor.operations_generated`.
- **Read model** — `reactor.readmodel.index.duration` (histogram, WRITE_READY → READ_READY).
- **Event bus** — `reactor.eventbus.events.emitted` with an `event.type` attribute.
- **Sync** — `reactor.sync.remotes` (active remote count) and `reactor.sync.dead_letters.added` with a `remote.name` attribute.

What makes the taxonomy genuinely useful is the event-mapping table: each metric is recorded from a named event, so a gap in a metric is a gap in an event.

| Event | Code | Records |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `JOB_PENDING` | 10001 | `queue.jobs.enqueued` |
| `JOB_RUNNING` | 10002 | `queue.jobs.dequeued` |
| `JOB_WRITE_READY` | 10003 | `executor.job.duration`, `total_processed`, `operations_generated` |
| `JOB_READ_READY` | 10004 | `readmodel.index.duration`, `job.total.duration`, `queue.jobs.completed` |
| `JOB_FAILED` | 10005 | `queue.jobs.failed`, `total_processed`, `job.total.duration` |
| `DEAD_LETTER_ADDED` | 20004 | `sync.dead_letters.added` |

Every one of them also increments `eventbus.events.emitted`.
